historical_evidence.finding: Defensive scheme change within games and across games (inferred labels) was untestable due to label error and near‑uniform transition matrices, implying label noise obscures real defensive adjustments.
Play‑type label backfill verification failed for several play types (e.g., PULL_UP) and showed PPP for PNR was unreliable; temporal consistency was good, but team identity and many labels failed.
Observed on‑ball defensive scheme labels could not be reliably derived from NBA match‑ups; only 14.9% of on‑ball possessions were labeled for DET and 3.3% for ORL, with missing switch data.
PPP differences for OTHER/DRIVE were found to be inflated or deflated due to foul leakage and low mapping rates (0.7% of possessions mapped to a real play type via initiation_type).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attempt to infer defensive scheme changes from noisy play‑type labels
failed_approaches.why: Label or classification error (LIM:label_or_classification_error); near‑uniform transition matrices indicated label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Back‑filling play‑type labels from league distributions
failed_approaches.why: Label or classification error; PNR PPP failed to meet league benchmarks, indicating artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Deriving on‑ball defensive scheme labels from NBA match‑ups
failed_approaches.why: Label error and small sample size (LIM:small_sample); low labeling rates.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using PPP as a proxy for real efficiency without accounting for foul leakage
failed_approaches.why: Artifact (C_artifact) due to foul leakage and low initiation_type mapping.

evidence_establishes: Labeling of DRIVE and PNR is noisy and may inflate or deflate PPP; PPP differences for other play types appear to be affected by foul leakage; labeling coverage for on‑ball defensive schemes is low and inconsistent.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR actually raises PNR PPP; whether the labeling system can reliably capture the temporal sequence of plays; whether other confounding factors can be controlled.
own_inferences: The data set contains systematic label errors that undermine confidence in PPP values for DRIVE and PNR; the sample size is large, but measurement error may dominate; confounding by team, opponent, and game situation is likely.
uncertainties: Exact magnitude of label error for DRIVE and PNR; potential hidden confounders linked to offensive or defensive match‑ups; feasibility of obtaining a validated set of play‑type labels.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved studies demonstrate that key play‑type labels (DRIVE and PNR) suffer from classification error and that PPP values may be biased by foul leakage. These findings raise doubt that the current data can answer the posed question reliably.

blocking_constraints.text: Systematic mislabeling of DRIVE and PNR play types and PPP values.
Potential correlation between preceding DRIVE play and other offensive/defensive factors that also influence PPP.
PPP is derived from potentially unreliable play‑type labels.
Although many possessions are available, measurement error may reduce effective power.

prior_work.summary: Prior studies have identified label errors and artifacts in play‑type PPP values, particularly for DRIVE and PNR, and have shown that inferred defensive adjustments are unreliable when labels are noisy.

risks.text: Systematic mislabeling of play types, especially DRIVE and PNR.
Unmeasured variables (team strength, defensive scheme) may correlate with both preceding DRIVE and PPP.
PPP as an outcome depends on potentially flawed play‑type labels.
High measurement noise could erode statistical power even with large sample sizes.

design.estimand: Average causal effect of a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR on the PPP of that PNR possession.
design.unit: individual possession where a PNR occurs.
design.sample: All possessions in NBA 2022‑23 through 2025‑26 regular season and playoffs with a PNR and a preceding teammate DRIVE identified from play‑by‑play.
design.power: A 90% power calculation with 80% power to detect a 0.05 PPP increase would require ~5,000 qualifying possessions; given label noise the effective sample is likely lower.
design.controls: Fixed effects for team, opponent, game period, possession number; covariates for shot distance, defensive match‑up minutes, and prior possession outcome; inclusion of a pre‑test for label reliability.
design.falsification: Test the same estimand for a non‑teammate preceding DRIVE (e.g., opponent DRIVE) to ensure no spurious effect; test for PNR following non‑DRIVE plays to confirm specificity.
design.multiplicity: Primary hypothesis only; secondary checks for other play types; no adjustment beyond Bonferroni for these few tests.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.05 after controlling for fixed effects; otherwise fail to reject.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play‑by‑play up to 2025‑26 season, derived possession records in graph database; labeling as per current inferred play‑type algorithm.
